parts.label: a
parts.text:

$\mathrm{f}(x) \equiv Ax+B+\dfrac{C(2x+3)}{x^2+3x+4}$
where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are integers to be found.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:

A1: $A=2$ May be seen in the long division or in the expression.
A1: Either $B=-6$ or $C=3$ stated or as part of the expression
A1: Both $B=-6$ and $C=3$ stated or as part of the expression
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $2x^3-4x-15=(Ax+B)(x^2+3x+4)+C(2x+3)\Rightarrow A=\ldots$ or $x^2+3x+4\overline{)2x^3+0x^2-4x-15}$ with quotient $2x\ldots$, $2x^3+\ldots$ M1
- $B=-6, C=3$ A1A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence, find
$\displaystyle\int_{3}^{5} \mathrm{f}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$
giving your answer in the form $p+\ln q$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to integrate their answer to (a), look for $x^n \to x^{n+1}$ at least once and $\dfrac{2x+3}{x^2+3x+4} \to k\ln(x^2+3x+4)$. Allow with letters used if values have not been found.

- $=4+\ln8$ A1

The functions f and g are defined by
$\mathrm{f}(x) = 5-\dfrac{4}{3x+2} \qquad x\geqslant 0$
$\mathrm{g}(x) = \left|4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right| \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the range of f
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: One correct end of range, though allow with $\geqslant$ or $<$ and $\ldots$ or $>$ (in correct direction) at the respective ends, and accept with $y$ instead of $\mathrm{f}(x)$, or even with $x$ for the M1.
A1: Correct range, allow with $y$ instead of $\mathrm{f}(x)$ or with other correct set notation (but use of $x$ is A0 unless in formal set notation). Accept as two separate inequalities.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Either $f(x)<5$ or $f(x)\geqslant3$ M1
- $3\leqslant f(x)<5$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) (i) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$
(ii) Write down the domain of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to make $x$ or a swapped $y$ the subject of the equation. Allow sign slips, but there should be a correct order of operations.
A1: Correct rule, must be in terms of $x$, accept equivalents and isw after a correct answer is seen. Do not be concerned with the lhs (accept $y=\ldots$ and even condone $\mathrm{f}(x)=\ldots$)
B1ft: Follow through on their answer to (a). Accept intervals or set notation answers. Do not accept e.g. $3\leqslant \mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)<5$ or with $y$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (i) $y=5-\frac{4}{3x+2}\Rightarrow\frac{4}{3x+2}=5-y\Rightarrow\frac{4}{5-y}=3x+2\Rightarrow x=\ldots$ M1
- $(f^{-1}(x))=\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{4}{5-x}-2\right)$ oe such as $\frac{4}{15-3x}-\frac{2}{3}$ or $\frac{2x-6}{15-3x}$ A1
- (ii) Domain is $3\leqslant x<5$ B1ft

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find $\mathrm{fg}(-\pi)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to evaluate g at $-\pi$ and substitutes into f. (Allow even if a negative value is found.) Evaluation of $\mathrm{g}(-\pi)$ must be attempted, not just substitution into the expression. They may find the expression for $\mathrm{fg}(x)$ first and substituted, in which case the trigonometric expression must be evaluated before the mark is awarded.
A1: Correct answer. Accept as decimal. Do not isw if they try to change to degrees.
Official notes (completeness pass):

- $=5-\frac{4}{6+2}=\frac{9}{2}$ A1

Figure 2 shows a sketch of the graph of $P$ against $t$.
The profit made by a company, $\pounds P$ million, $t$ years after the company started trading, is modelled by the equation
$P = \dfrac{4t-1}{10} + \dfrac{3}{4}\ln\left[\dfrac{t+1}{(2t+1)^2}\right]$
The graph of $P$ against $t$ is shown in Figure 2.
According to the model,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that exactly one year after it started trading, the company had made a loss of approximately $\pounds830\,000$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to substitute $t=1$ into the given formula. Allow if there is a slip but an attempt at substitution is seen, or allow for sight of awrt $-0.828\ldots$
A1*: Correct value for $P(1)$ seen to at least 2 s.f. if substitution has been shown, or at least 3 s.f. if no substitution was shown, followed by suitable conclusion that it is a loss of approximately $\pounds830\,000$, though accept awrt $\pounds830\,000$. Must mention "loss" and include units ($\pounds$ or pounds). Negative value given is A0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $P(1)=\frac{4-1}{10}+\frac{3}{4}\ln\left(\frac{2}{3^2}\right)$ $(=-0.828\ldots)$ M1
- $P(1)=-0.828\ldots$ (which is negative so a loss of £0.828 million,) so approximately £830 000 loss. A1*

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A manager of the company wants to know the value of $t$ for which $P=0$
(b) Show that this value of $t$ occurs in the interval $[6,7]$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts both $P(6)$ and $P(7)$ with at least one correct to 1 s.f. rounded or truncated. A tighter interval could be used but must contain the root ($6.31487\ldots$)
A1: Both correct to 1 s.f. rounded or truncated with suitable conclusion made. Must mention sign change and continuity as well as conclusion about root in the interval.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $P(6)=-0.08799\ldots$ and $P(7)=0.1975\ldots$ M1
- There is a sign change and hence as P is continuous on [6,7], so the root for t lies in [6,7]. A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Show that the equation $P=0$ can be expressed in the form
$t = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{15}{8}\ln\left[\dfrac{(2t+1)^2}{t+1}\right]$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to isolate $t$ from the $\dfrac{4t-1}{10}$ after setting equal to zero.
A1*: Correct work to reach the given answer with no incorrect work seen and at least one intermediate step with either $\alpha t=\ldots$ reached or with the power law applied on the ln term (need not see the power explicitly used, but must have been applied correctly).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $P=0\Rightarrow\frac{4t-1}{10}=-\frac{3}{4}\ln\left(\frac{t+1}{(2t+1)^2}\right)\Rightarrow t=\ldots$ M1

find the value of $t_2$ and the value of $t_6$, giving your answers to 3 decimal places.
(3)
